newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals hover nervously at support.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals hover nervously at support.

text.p: Gold kept its balance at a critical support level on Friday after a week of pummelling from all quarters, dealers said.
But the market was overwhelmingly bearish and threatened to topple to fresh lows for the year in the near term.
"The market looks weak and vulnerable. Everyone is having a go," a dealer said. A spate of selling this week has been linked to gold producers, a European central bank and investment funds.

Bullion fixed at $377.60 an ounce, compared to $377.20 in morning and down about $5.00 since the start of the week. Trading was quiet as many European markets were close for the All Saints Day holiday.
"At the moment gold is perilously close to key support at $376.90," brokers GNI said in a report, referring to the 18-month low gold hit at the start of October.
"If this goes the price could drop to $370 pretty quickly," the report added.
Prices dipped lower briefly, then recovered, following U.S. payroll and unemployment data midday which confirmed no inflationary pressures in the economy.
The news was seen further diminishing investor interest in the precious metals, a traditional hedge against price rises.
"It doesn't matter what the news is when the market is like this. All news is bearish," a dealer said.
Ironically, the cost of borrowing gold surged higher this week, particularly three-month gold lease rates, which indicated that supplies of metal available for borrowing were tight.
The expectation that gold miners planned to sell more metal in the near term was behind the move, dealers said.
Producers typically sell gold which they have not yet mined by borrowing metal from central banks to sell. They pay the bank back once their own gold has been mined and refined.
The other precious metals shared gold's fragile hold on nearby support levels.
Silver was seven cents lower at $4.78/$4.80 an ounce after dropping with gold overnight, and was seen eventually targetting levels as low as $4.50, analysts said.
"Silver is selling in sympathy with gold, which is why it isn't moving lower at the same pace," a dealer said.
Platinum was trading at $380.00/$381.00, down $0.50. Its fate was likely linked with gold, dealers said.
"If gold goes, platinum may follow it," a dealer said.
